key_insight: Drift-diffusion optimization shows that Cu2SiSe3 and Cu2SnS3 ternary chalcogenides can work as viable solar absorbers, with tandem integration delivering the highest performance.
engineering_relevance: These results suggest low-complexity Cu-based chalcogenides could be engineered into cost-effective single-junction or tandem photovoltaic stacks for higher efficiency devices.
method: Simulated single-junction solar cells with drift-diffusion modeling.
Optimized absorber thickness, intrinsic carrier concentration, defect density, and interfacial band alignment.
Evaluated a two-terminal tandem using Cu2SiSe3 as the top cell and Cu2SnS3 as the bottom cell.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 18.13% efficiency for Cu2SiSe3, 15.59% for Cu2SnS3, and 24.1% for the tandem device, based on simulated electrical metrics including VOC, JSC, and fill factor.
watch_item: The gains are simulation-based, so real-device performance may be limited by materials quality, interface defects, and fabrication control.
paper_title: Photovoltaic Possibility of Cu2SiSe3 and Cu2SnS3 Ternary Chalcogenides- Single Junction to Tandem Architecture
